decision.explanation: The evidence from the MyPathway study (pmid-29320312) supports the claim. Specifically, the study evaluated patients with HER2 (ERBB2) mutations treated with the combination of trastuzumab and pertuzumab. Among the subgroup of patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC), 3 out of 14 (21%) achieved a partial response (PR), and 3 had stable disease (SD) > 120 days. This demonstrates that ERBB2 mutations are predictive of sensitivity/response to the trastuzumab and pertuzumab combination in NSCLC. The evidence aligns with the claim's disease (Lung Non-small Cell Carcinoma), molecular profile (ERBB2 Mutation), therapies (Trastuzumab, Pertuzumab), therapy interaction (Combination), variant origin (Somatic, implied by tumor mutations), and significance (sensitivity/response).

citations.quote: The phase 2a MyPathway study assigned patients with HER2, EGFR, BRAF or SHH alterations to treatment with pertuzumab plus trastuzumab, erlotinib, vemurafenib, or vismodegib, respectively. Among thirty-six patients that received treatment with trastuzumab plus pertuzumab because of a HER2 mutation (without amplification/overexpression) four patients (11%; 95% CI, 3% to 26%) had objective responses.

Fourteen of the 36 patients with HER2-mutated tumors had NSCLC (adenocarcinoma, n = 13; adenosquamous, n = 1); in this group, three patients (21%; 95% CI, 5% to 51%) had PR and three had SD > 120 days. Only one of the other 22 patients with HER2-mutated tumors responded to treatment with pertuzumab plus trastuzumab (biliary cancer).
